item.title: Charles Barkley Steals March Madness 2026: Weight Loss, Bold Predictions, and Unforgettable Moments
item.description:
Every March, Charles Barkley transforms from NBA analyst into college basketball’s most entertaining commentator — and in 2026, he’s doing it with a noticeably slimmer frame, razor-sharp humor, and predictions that have fans buzzing.

Key Takeaways:

  • Barkley has lost over 60 pounds using GLP-1 medication combined with exercise, dropping from 352 to around 290 pounds
  • He’s delivering memorable broadcast moments alongside Dick Vitale during the 2026 NCAA Tournament
  • His Auburn Tigers missed the 68-team field, leading to hilarious on-air jabs at coach Bruce Pearl
  • Barkley “guaranteed” Auburn will face a March Madness Cinderella next season
  • He praised High Point’s stunning upset over Wisconsin and their coach Flynn Caymann’s leadership

Charles Barkley’s Weight Loss Transformation Turns Heads

Before the basketball talk, there’s something fans can’t stop noticing: Barkley looks different. The 62-year-old NBA Hall of Famer has undergone a remarkable physical transformation that has become a storyline of its own.

item.title: McNeese Basketball Returns to March Madness: Cowboys Eye Another 5-12 Upset
item.description:
McNeese Basketball Returns to March Madness: Cowboys Eye Another 5-12 Upset

Key Takeaways:

  • 12-seed McNeese faces 5-seed Vanderbilt on March 19 in Oklahoma City
  • The Cowboys upset 5-seed Clemson in last year’s first round as a 12-seed
  • Viral student manager Amir “Aura” Khan and his boombox are back for another March run
  • This is a classic 5-12 matchup — historically one of the most upset-prone seeds in the tournament

What are the odds that lightning strikes twice in the same spot? McNeese basketball is betting on exactly that as the Cowboys return to the NCAA Tournament with the same script that made them America’s Cinderella last March.

item.title: WVU Basketball Big 12 Tournament: Mountaineers' NCAA Hopes on the Line
item.description:
WVU basketball needs a miracle run — and they know it. The seventh-seeded West Virginia Mountaineers enter the Big 12 Tournament at 18-13, sitting firmly on the outside of the NCAA Tournament bubble. Their only path to March Madness likely runs through Kansas City.

Key Takeaways

  • WVU enters the Big 12 Tournament as the 7th seed with an 18-13 record
  • The Mountaineers are off Joe Lunardi’s NCAA Tournament bubble
  • Key wins this season: Kansas, BYU, and Pitt (71-49)
  • Senior guard Honor Huff earned All-Big 12 Honorable Mention
  • WVU women’s basketball won the Big 12 title and may host NCAA games

WVU Basketball’s Roller-Coaster Season Under Ross Hodge

First-year head coach Ross Hodge has navigated a season full of extremes. The highs have been exhilarating — none more than a 71-49 demolition of rival Pitt that Hodge says he’ll “never forget for as long as I live.”
